extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and institutions applying for NCI Cancer Moonshot funding (and peer reviewers/administrators evaluating those applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and requirements used by NCI for reviewing Cancer Moonshot funding applications, describing program-wide expectations (core features, policy requirements) and specific review considerations for Moonshot initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong commitment to collaborative research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the Four Core Features required across all Cancer Moonshot funding. Applications are expected to demonstrate collaboration (e.g., multi-investigator, multi-institutional partnerships) as a central element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace of open access publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core feature across all Cancer Moonshot funding. Applicants should plan for and commit to open-access dissemination of published research results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust policy of complete data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust policy of complete data sharing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core feature across all Cancer Moonshot awards. Applications should describe data sharing policies/practices and how data will be made available in accordance with program expectations (see also PADS policy entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on elimination of cancer health disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: Intense focus on the elimination of cancer health disparities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core program expectation that proposals address cancer health disparities; proposals should describe how their work will reduce or eliminate disparities in cancer outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard peer review process (written critique and overall impact scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications receive a written critique as part of scientific peer review; applications may undergo selection where only those deemed highest scientific and technical merit (generally top half) are discussed and assigned an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the review workflow: written critiques for all applications; discussion and scoring typically reserved for those in the top half by initial triage. Applicants should expect written feedback and that only higher-merit applications may be scored/discussed in study section; scientific and technical merit drives selection for discussion and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technical merit / overall impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated for scientific and technical merit and assigned an overall impact score when discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit program-level scoring criterion: proposals should demonstrate high scientific rigor, significance, innovation, and approach to rank among the highest scientific and technical merit for discussion and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and Inclusion efforts within centers
rubrics_metrics.description: NCI measures and evaluates efforts to achieve diversity within NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers. Four aims: (1) Having the right infrastructure; (2) Growing the pipelines of future clinicians and researchers; (3) Recruiting individuals from under-represented populations; (4) Accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants (or centers) should document infrastructure to support diversity, plans to develop pipelines into clinical/research careers, active recruitment strategies for underrepresented groups, and mechanisms for accountability (metrics, reporting). This is a specialized criterion for Moonshot funding evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access and Data Sharing (PADS) Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: PADS policy applicable to all Cancer Moonshot funding applications submitted on or after October 1, 2017; requires all applicants to submit a PADS plan describing how they will meet goals for immediate public release of published research results and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a PADS plan is mandatory for affected applications. The plan should detail mechanisms and timelines for immediate public release of publications and data, and how the project will comply with program expectations for openness and data sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Pediatric Cancer Initiative priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on pediatric oncology innovations (e.g., DCI / RACE for Children Act) as part of Cancer Moonshot specific initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals targeting pediatric cancer should demonstrate clear alignment with initiative goals, applicable regulatory/legislative frameworks (e.g., RACE for Children Act), and relevance to pediatric oncology innovation priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for early-stage investigators from underrepresented groups (CMSDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: CANCER Moonshot Scholars Diversity Program (CMSDP): R01 mechanism supporting early-stage investigators from underrepresented groups doing cancer-relevant research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CMSDP opportunities, emphasis is placed on candidate eligibility (early-stage investigators from underrepresented groups), the cancer relevance of the research, and fit with the R01 mechanism. Applications should address how they meet the program's diversity and career-stage objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with other Moonshot initiatives and networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance to other Moonshot initiatives (Drug Resistance and Sensitivity Network, Adult Immunotherapy Network, ATOM Initiative, Cancer Immunotherapy Translational Network, Patient-Derived Models Repository, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate how proposed work leverages, contributes to, or integrates with existing Moonshot networks/resources or initiative-specific goals. Use of and interaction with these resources may be favorably considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational potential to clinic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Special Review Considerations. Proposals should articulate clear paths to clinical translation, expected timelines, and evidence that findings could be moved toward clinical application or trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and community engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A special review consideration: applications should describe meaningful engagement with patients and community stakeholders (design, recruitment, dissemination, priorities) and how engagement informs the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health equity considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will consider whether proposals address health equity (e.g., inclusion of diverse populations, analyses of disparate impacts, strategies to reduce inequities). This aligns with the core feature prioritizing elimination of cancer health disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-institutional collaboration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighted as a special review consideration and related to the core feature of collaboration. Applications involving multiple institutions should describe roles, management plans, data/resource sharing, and the added value of the collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing Moonshot networks/resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will consider whether proposals effectively use and integrate existing Moonshot infrastructures, datasets, or consortia (which can enhance feasibility, reproducibility, and impact). Applicants should describe planned use of these resources.
